For ten years, I have been organizing business visits for international companies, and I always give my clients the same three pieces of advice. First, plan the itinerary around the flight, not around your calendar. Many visitors arrive after a long layover, with bad jet lag, so never put an important meeting on the first morning. Second, expect a hiccup. A flight is late, a restaurant loses your reservation, a driver gets lost. The hiccup is not the real problem. The real problem is having no plan B. So always keep the number of a second venue, and decide who will make the calls. Third, give your visitor something they cannot get by email. Let them see your work first-hand: a farm, a warehouse, a factory. That is what they remember. And when the visit is over, have a short debrief with your team in the same week, while everything is fresh. Write down three lessons learned, and use them for the next visit.

Last year, a buyer from Osaka came to visit us in Santos. On the first night, I took her to a famous restaurant, but when we arrived, the manager said that they had no record of our reservation. I was so embarrassed. My buyer just smiled and said that she was very hungry, and that any place was fine. We walked to a small fish restaurant on the beach, and it was the best evening of the week. On the last day, she told me that the dinner on the beach was her favorite moment of the trip. Since then, she has been buying coffee from us every season, and every time she calls, she asks me, you still remember that beach, don't you? That visit taught me something important. Clients do not remember the perfect plan. They remember how you handled the hiccup.

Mr. Becker arrived on Monday after a long layover in Lisbon. Because of his jet lag, we changed the itinerary on short notice. On Tuesday, there was a hiccup: the restaurant lost our reservation, so we found another venue. On Wednesday, he saw our traceability system first-hand. On Friday, we had a debrief and wrote down the lessons learned. Since then, we have been working on a checklist for future visits.
